claims.text: Satisfying all statistical criteria of algorithmic fairness simultaneously is impossible unless base rates are equal across relevant groups.
Statistical criteria of algorithmic fairness, except calibration, are not necessary conditions for fairness.
Purported statistical fairness criteria (except calibration) can be simultaneously violated by a manifestly fair and uniquely optimal predictive algorithm.
A manifestly fair and uniquely optimal predictive algorithm can violate statistical fairness criteria even when base rates are equal across groups.

evidence.description: a series of impossibility results shows that this is impossible, unless base rates are equal across the relevant groups.
I argue that none of the purported criteria, except for a calibration criterion, are necessary conditions for fairness
they can all be simultaneously violated by a manifestly fair and uniquely optimal predictive algorithm
even when base rates are equal.

methodologies.name: Philosophical and theoretical analysis
methodologies.description: Conceptual argument and counterexample analysis showing that optimal fair predictive algorithms violate statistical criteria of fairness.

limitations.text: Statistical criteria of fairness cannot all be satisfied simultaneously when base rates differ across groups.
